title: Controls of weather and climate
competency: Explain how latitude, altitude, the sea, clouds and ocean currents control climate.

keywords.def: Factors that affect the elements of weather and climate: latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, cloud cover, ocean currents, wind, air pressure.
The rate at which air temperature falls with height: normally 6.4°C per 1000 m.

en.text: Controls are factors that make the elements of climate uneven. Near the equator the sun is overhead and it is hot; towards the poles rays are slanting and it is cold. Temperature falls about 6.4°C per 1000 m of height (lapse rate). Coasts are cooler and wetter; clouds reduce radiation; warm and cold ocean currents change coastal climate.

screens.ask: Both are near the equator, but Mount Kilimanjaro has snow on top while the plains below are hot. Why?
opts: The sun never reaches the top
The mountain is near the pole
screens.after: Temperature drops about 6.4°C for every 1000 m you climb. High enough, it is below freezing.

screens.title: Controls
paras: Controls of weather and climate are factors that affect its elements.
They make the elements uneven over the earth's surface.
Major controls: latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, cloud cover, ocean currents, wind and air pressure.

screens.title: The controls
items: Distance from the equator. Overhead sun at the equator = hot; slanting rays at the poles = cold.
Temperature falls 6.4°C per 1000 m (normal lapse rate). Ethiopia's highlands show this.
Coasts are cooler and wetter; the centres of continents have a large temperature range.
Clouds reduce sunshine reaching the ground and heat leaving it.
Warm currents: hot and moist. Cold currents: cool and dry coastal lands.

screens.title: The overhead sun
paras: The sun is overhead only between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.
Overhead at the Tropic of Cancer on June 21 and at the Tropic of Capricorn on December 21.
At the March and September equinoxes it is overhead at the equator.
screens.note: Equinox: the sun is directly above the equator (March 21 and September 23).
